messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy started to eu-west and us-east (blue->green) for route inference.v2 at 1768001111. Canary in eu-west only.

sandeep (oncall): getting a few alerts — 502 spikes from eu-west canary. paging me. investigating now.

jamie - eng: looking at canary logs, seeing high 5xx from gRPC shard: 
```
2026-03-15T12:05:32Z ERROR inference: downstream stream reset (RST_STREAM) request_id=abc123 shard=eu-west-2
2026-03-15T12:05:34Z WARN  kvcache: not found prefix miss key=conversation_kv_....
```

marta - infra: checking edge -> origin routing. I can see a subset of eu-west edge POPs resolving to old-green IPs due to stale DNS responses still cached at a few CDN nodes. DNS weight for eu-west was flipped as part of the rollout.

jamie - eng: interesting — the errors line up with clients hitting green where new model config expects a different tokenizer path. fallback errors cause 502.

incident-bot: @sandeep (oncall) — incident created: GEO-ROLLUP-1768001111, severity=P2, started=1768001111. Pages: sandeep, marta.

kevin (support): We have one paying customer (acme-corp) reporting requests failing intermittently. They've escalated to priority. On a call with their infra.

sandeep (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) flip feature flag kill-switch for model-switch (prevent new config usage) 2) stop rollout in eu-west 3) change DNS weight to send 100% to old-blue until we confirm.

jamie - eng: I can toggle the feature flag now. Command: 
```
# toggle via flagctl
flagctl set inference_model_v2_enabled false --env=eu-west --metadata "incident:1768001111"
```

marta - infra: i'm checking CDN caches and DNS TTLs. TTL on the record is 60s but some upstream caches have >5m. I'll push a shorter emergency record by adding a low-TTL override in our control plane and triggering cache purge for affected POPs.

marta - infra: running: 
```
# set emergency override
infractl dns override set inference.eu-west.example.net --weight=0 --ttl=10 --note "incident 1768001111"
# purge edge caches for eu-west POPs
cdnctl purge --filter pop=eu-west-*
```

jamie - eng: feature flag toggle done. Monitoring logs for immediate drop in 502s.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused (eu-west) by manual intervention.

sandeep (oncall): confirm kevin — are acme-corp requests improving?

kevin (support): on the call — their traffic looks better now but still a few fails. They reported last fail ~30s ago.

marta - infra: purge completed for most POPs, but two legacy caches (carrier proxies) still show old A records. I'm going to add an IP-based routing rule at the LB to nudge traffic off the green instances while TTLs clear.

jamie - eng: while infra does LB work, i'm opening a canary rollback for the model artifact on eu-west green so any direct hits to green will get the previous artifact. Rolling back canary package.

jamie - eng: rollback command: 
```
deployctl release rollback --service inference --to-tag=blue-20260220 --region=eu-west --canary-only
```

marta - infra: LB rule applied: if src_ip in known-carrier-range then route -> blue-backend. This catches the stubborn traffic.

sandeep (oncall): status update 12:12Z: 502s down ~90% vs peak. ACME says errors nearly gone. Still monitoring for any other customer impact.

incident-bot: Update recorded: mitigation=feature_flag_kill, dns_override, lb_rule, canary_rollback.

alice (customer-success): messaging ready for ACME: short note that a partial rollout caused intermittent failures, we paused the rollout and rolled back canary; continue to monitor. Shall I send now?

kevin (support): yes send the customer note (cc sandeep, alice). Include ETA for full rollout reattempt: TBD after postmortem.

jamie - eng: logs now (sample): 
```
12:13:01 INFO  model-loader: loaded model blue-20260220 OK
12:13:30 INFO  router: route change enforced -> 100% blue in eu-west
12:14:05 WARN  grpc: transient RSTs, flood reduced
```

marta - infra: dns TTLs are now settling. I've set monitoring alerts for any residual POPs resolving to green.

sandeep (oncall): moving to recovery: stop rollout globally until root cause confirmed. Assigning owners: jamie -> rollback verification and canary artifact audit; marta -> DNS/CDN cache analysis and carrier cache outreach; kevin/alice -> customer comms and incident updates.

sandeep (oncall): I'll hand off on-call to marta for overnight watch at 12:30Z. Handoff notes: rollout paused, canary rolled back, feature flag disabled for eu-west, LB rule in place, ACME stable.

marta - infra: taking handoff. I'll keep a short checklist in the incident doc and run periodic checks on POP resolution for 2 hours.

incident-bot: On-call handoff recorded: from=sandeep to=marta at 1768002200.

alice (customer-success): sent customer note to ACME (copied kevin, sandeep). They replied: "Thanks, we'll keep an eye on it and appreciate the quick rollback."

kevin (support): closing customer support loop for now. Will reopen if they see regressions.

sandeep (oncall): final ops note before handoff: collect kernel of reproduction — jamie please capture exact model artifact diff (tokenizer path change) and we will include in the postmortem root cause.

jamie - eng: captured diffs, pushing to internal incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/GEO-ROLLUP-1768001111/diffs.txt

marta - infra: will follow up with the CDN/carrier contacts for cache expiry anomaly. Adding timeline entries to the incident board.

incident-bot: Incident GEO-ROLLUP-1768001111 status=mitigated, severity downgraded to P3, assigned=marta, notes="monitoring; customer notified".

sandeep (oncall): leaving handoff. If anything spikes, ping #pager and page oncall. Good job team :thumbsup:

marta - infra: acknowledged. Going to monitor until 14:30Z then open a postmortem draft.

--- end of thread ---
